comments.text: Prepares the bus and reads the single-letter disk file selected by $0D1B. The caller increments the index between the five files in a stage.
Sets the disk parameters and filename, calls KERNAL LOAD with A clear, then returns on success. On carry set the code copies the file index to the border and stays in its error loop.
Receives the selected file index while the load error loop changes the border.
Sets logical file 1, device 8 and secondary address 1 for an absolute-address disk load.
Adds the stage file index at $0D1B to the address $0950 and passes the resulting one-byte filename to SETNAM.
The ASCII letters A through Y are the filenames in five groups of five. $0936 passes the address of one letter to the KERNAL.
Disables sprites and maps KERNAL ROM in before the load.
Low byte of the requested destination loaded into X before KERNAL LOAD.
High byte of the requested destination loaded into Y before KERNAL LOAD. Secondary address 1 makes the PRG header supply the load address.
BASIC directory-style records with next-line RAM pointers, block counts and PETSCII filenames. The stage entries list C/D/E through W/X/Y, three files per stage. The line links end at $0C9D.
Boundary inside the stored BASIC-style directory. The fragment at $0CA2 encodes this address as a call target, and the resident snapshot holds directory data here.
Stored filename and block-count records in the directory suffix. $0CA8 encodes a call to $0B59 inside a copied code fragment, even though those bytes lie inside the directory.
Zero next-line pointer ends the embedded catalog. The following byte is $22.

Code fragment after the embedded catalog. The calls to $EDDD in its second path send three address or command fields and a 32-byte buffer through the KERNAL serial routine. Runtime use of this fragment is open.
Sixteen stored zero bytes between the copied serial fragment and the bank-switch instructions.
Nine bytes at the end of LOADER call $0E4F, disable interrupts, write $35 to the processor port and load $AE before SEC. Runtime use of the fragment is open.
Masks $01 through $80 set one sprite's ninth X bit in $D010.
Eight inverse masks clear one sprite's ninth X bit.
Set to three during startup and decremented by the life icon routine.
Least significant pair of score digits in packed BCD.
Middle pair of score digits, including the carry from the low byte.
Most significant packed BCD score pair.
Low pair of the pending score increment, added by $2971 and then cleared.
High pair of the pending score increment.
Zero-based stage index multiplied by five to select its file group.
Index into the stage event pointer table at $3B2C.
Cleared during actor and death setup and set after the screen and map changes at $1AAE. The rest of this initial data span ends at the file index.
Clears at the start of the four-actor frame update, before the next byte and the file index field.
Index into the A–Y disk filename table.
Gates the Hall of Fame and first story message, and is set before stage animation.
Coarse horizontal scroll in character columns.

High byte of the current tile map row pointer.

Flag gating the IRQ scroll routine at $C003.
Copy of the action-header scroll request, combined with actor occupancy to gate scrolling.
Address used by two absolute BITs to delay the playfield raster register writes.
Set after the position check when the target does not block scrolling.
Set at the first or last map column. The movement routine tests it before constraining player X.
Copy of the low orientation bit used to choose positive or mirrored X offsets.
Signed horizontal step extracted from offset 2 of the animation entry, negated when mirrored.
Signed vertical step read from offset 3 of the animation entry.
Updated X position used as the origin for this actor's constituent sprites.
Updated Y position used as the base of the sprite Y offsets.
Horizontal offset of first hardware sprite from the actor origin after mirroring.
Vertical offset of first hardware sprite.

Vertical offset of second hardware sprite.
Horizontal offset of third hardware sprite.
Vertical offset of third hardware sprite.
Horizontal offset of fourth hardware sprite.
Vertical offset of fourth hardware sprite.
Horizontal offset of fifth hardware sprite.
Vertical offset of fifth hardware sprite.
Current frame sprite count, also used as a loop counter when writing hardware coordinates.
Captures the hardware slot from the actor record at $267E. The remaining initial bytes before the mask table are zero in COD1.
Masks added for the player's upper hardware slots after its frame update.
Masks for the first auxiliary actor's assigned sprite slots.
Masks for the second auxiliary actor's sprite slots.
Masks added for the stage actor's sprite allocation.
Gates dispatch through $3B17.
Gates the action selection at $11CA.
Gates updates for the two auxiliary actor records.
Gates the stage-specific opponent and its stage sprite library selection.
Gates the update routine at $36DA.

Allows calls to the common four-actor animation routine at $12E3.
Gates the raster-synchronized sprite upload at $25D9.
Gates the player-attack testing routine at $3192.
Gates the player X bound routine at $3ACE.
Gates whether $2FFC can limit scrolling when an opponent is close.

Gates the death and life-counter handler at $3C73.
Gates the periodic addition and redraw at $2971.
Gates the stage tile change check at $1A48.
If clear, the music update returns before ticking the prescaler.
Allows an inactive auxiliary slot to tick its spawn counter.
Set in the second stage transition at $3B95 and cleared by the death setup at $36AE.
Loads file indices 0 through 4, enables the display and seeds three lives and stage index zero before the first stage setup.
Starts the shared stage setup after either boot or an overlay load. Clears actor slots, initialises VIC and IRQ control, restores panel display and sets map origin.
Tests the hit-detection enable byte before calling $3192. Subsequent flags gate player bounds, actor scroll blocking, off-screen actors, death handling, score and tile writes.
Selects VIC bank $4000 through CIA2, screen base $5000 and multicolour character mode.
The video setup stores the old CIA2 data direction into this immediate operand, then restores it after selecting the VIC bank.
Installs $0F32 as IRQ and $0F50 for NMI and reset in RAM, then changes the processor port to bank out KERNAL while leaving I/O visible.
Sets the tile and colour row bases to $5400 and $6700 and clears fine horizontal scroll.
Installs the RAM IRQ vector at $0314, enables VIC raster interrupts and schedules $0F51 for raster line $61.
Saves A, X and Y. A VIC raster interrupt is acknowledged and passed to the JSR operand at $0F46. The routine acknowledges CIA1 and restores registers before RTI.
Low operand of the JSR at $0F45. Each raster handler installs the other handler here.
High operand of the interrupt callback. Following it, the handler acknowledges CIA1 and restores the saved registers.
Queues $0F90 at line $FC, sets stage multicolours and merges the fine-scroll value into $D016 before calling the scroll update.
Self-modified opcode. $8D writes the computed VIC character base to $D018. $AD instead reads it when the panel charset must remain selected.
Queues $0F51 at line $61, selects the panel charset at $4800, clears fine scroll and calls the sound updates.
Starts the entrance script and updates the player actor and sprites repeatedly until the player X coordinate reaches $57. Sets the input-enabled flag on completion.
Busy-waits in nested counters with Y initially $0A and X reloaded to $FB.
Writes six zero glyphs to the score and seeds the initial timer characters with 89.
Writes seventeen full-width bar glyphs to the panel address passed in $DD/$DE.
Writes the two character codes at $7A09 and $7A0A through the stage-specific screen pointer in $7A00.
Draws three life silhouettes across three panel rows at two-cell spacing.
Number of previously removed life silhouettes used to index the next set of panel cells.
Increments the lost-life icon index, erases its cells across three rows and decrements the lives value.
Clears both 40-byte actor records at $164F and $16C4.

A CIA1 port B value other than $FF clears the timer and scroll enable. After seven delays, polls until another non-$FF value, runs two more delays and re-enables the timer. Live RUN/STOP checks reached both branches.
Sets two actor records inactive, giving them different base sprite pointers and VIC slots.
Enables multicolour sprites, establishes shared and player colours, and seeds the player actor's script, coordinates, health and hardware allocation.
Saved comparison result from the current action header's behavior class.
Byte 4 of the selected action header, used by opponent logic and attack response.
Last stick mask used by $1229 to decide whether to keep or change an action.
Reads the player actor header, updates the horizontal input transform for right or left facing, and compares the stick state with the current actor action.
Two zero bytes between the input selector return and the four-actor update.
Updates the four actor records and combines their hardware enable masks in $1370.
Low-byte sentinel flag used with a page check before reversing the actor.
Sum by OR of the actor sprite masks, sent to $D015 at the sprite update.
Interprets the current animation step and its frame descriptor, copies sprite indices, calculates per-sprite positions with horizontal mirroring, and advances the step when its tick counter expires.
Adds five to the actor's animation cursor. A zero high byte in the next frame pointer returns the record to its idle dispatch state, otherwise the next step supplies the frame duration.
Shift register combining the successive low-bit products for the multiply at $1627. The nearby bytes hold inputs and returned low and high result bytes.
The initial X argument, shifted right to expose one multiplier bit each pass.
The Y argument, added to the accumulator on set multiplier bits.
Copy of the product low byte returned in X.
Copy of the product high byte returned in Y.
Eight shift-and-add passes compute the unsigned product of X and Y, returning low in X and high in Y.
Beginning of the player record. Its first five positions hold hardware sprite indices and byte 5 holds the first VIC cache pointer.
Orientation in bit zero, separate hit flags in bits five and six, and death flag in bit seven.
Player record byte 7 gates animation and rendering.
Current action byte. $FF requests a fresh action in the entrance and interlude logic.
Player's base X position in half-pixel coordinate units.
Player Y origin, five pairs of computed sprite coordinates, count and first hardware slot, and the three descriptor fields copied at $13AB through $13C1.
Remaining ticks before the player animation reads its next five-byte script entry.
Player health at actor offset $20, seeded to $40 and reduced in hit handling.
Low byte of the player's action header pointer.
High byte of the player's action header pointer.
Low byte of the currently selected animation cursor.
High byte of the player animation cursor.
Beginning of the first shared opponent record, with its frame indices before the VIC base pointer.
First cache slot for the first auxiliary actor, adjusted by the sprite allocation logic.
Faces left or right from bit zero, toggled during transition.
Animation and draw enable for the first auxiliary actor. Subsequent bytes before the coordinate hold action and step state.
Base X coordinate of the first auxiliary actor.
First auxiliary actor Y followed by its computed sprite positions.
Number of hardware sprites in the active first auxiliary actor frame.
First VIC sprite slot for the first auxiliary actor, followed by its frame and attack attributes.
Tick count for this auxiliary actor's current animation step, before health and type.
State used to index the common auxiliary header table.
Low byte of the first auxiliary action header pointer.
High byte of the first auxiliary action header.
Low byte of the first auxiliary animation cursor.
High byte of the first auxiliary animation cursor.
Start of the second shared opponent's frame indices and cache pointer.
Facing and status flags for the second auxiliary slot.
Animation enable for the second auxiliary actor, followed by its action progress fields.
Base X of the second auxiliary actor. Its remaining record holds Y, sprite positions, hit fields and pointers in the same offsets as the first actor.
Stage opponent frame indices and first sprite-cache pointer.
Facing and hit flags for the stage opponent.
Controls drawing and updating of the stage opponent.
Action state, including $FF when a new stage-specific header is needed.
Base X, also adjusted when the map scrolls.
Base Y and sprite coordinate components for the stage opponent.
Tick countdown until the next stage opponent script step.

High byte of the stage actor's current header pointer.

Low five bits of the inverted CIA1 port, with possible horizontal remapping before storage at $16ED.
Copy of the player facing bit. Enables left and right exchange in the joystick reader.
Normalized five-bit joystick mask used by the action lookup.
Inverts active-low bits at $DC00, keeps the five direction and fire bits, and exchanges left and right when the facing flag at $16EC is set.
The first of 32 pointer words indexed by the decoded stick bits at $124C. Index zero selects the idle header at $210F.
Low byte of the header pointer for joystick mask $01. The stage and hit/death paths can replace it.
High byte of the action header selected by joystick up.

High byte of the fire-alone entry. The next fifteen words cover $11 through $1F.
The byte $17 lies after the 32 joystick action pointers and before the copied disk routine.
Return instruction immediately before the relocated copy of the stage load helper.
Relocated counterpart of $090C, passing filename and disk arguments before LOAD. Its filename address arithmetic still points to the resident $0950 table.
Self-written file number used alongside the relocated border loop.
Relocated version of the logical file and drive setup at $092D.

An RTS byte immediately after the facing routine's tail jump.
Selects which of the two auxiliary slots is being updated.
Result of the active auxiliary actor sprite count used by the allocator.
Working counter shared by the two auxiliary actor updates, with separate saved values for each.

Saved spawn countdown for the second auxiliary opponent.
Updates records at $1676 and $169D one at a time, passing their independent counters through $17DD.
Tests actor readiness, animation and behaviour flags before choosing a spawn or update path. Reloads the spawn delay from $7A10.

Sixteen consecutive source bytes for the actor initialisation code reached from $1889.
Four actor header pointers. The two-byte index from $1697 selects one of these words in $3137.
Restores timer digits to 99, clears the coarse scroll and stage event index, and enables the main stage update flags.
At the stage column stored at $7A0D, tests the active script's type byte and can write replacement character bytes to the screen and its backing map.
Three zero bytes between the preceding map patch routine and the first referenced animation descriptor at $1AE3.

68 animation descriptors referenced by common actor streams, from $1AE3 through $1EBF. In each, the count and indices select hardware sprites, followed by per-sprite offsets and collision fields consumed by $1371.

32 animation descriptors referenced by common actor streams, from $1ECC through $20C6. In each, the count and indices select hardware sprites, followed by per-sprite offsets and collision fields consumed by $1371.
Reads by index during actor hit testing. The common animation descriptors before this table have frame pointers in the $21FF–$25D6 scripts.
Pairs of relative attack X and Y coordinates. $31E3 and $31EA fetch the two bytes at twice the attack index.
48 five-byte headers. The first two bytes point to a common animation stream. Byte +2 feeds the scroll request at $12AD and byte +4 distinguishes the special action kind at $125E.
8 common animation streams, with entry points $21FF through $228F. Each five-byte step gives a frame address, signed coordinate deltas and duration. A zero pointer stops the sequence.
8 common animation streams, with entry points $22CD through $2369. Each five-byte step gives a frame address, signed coordinate deltas and duration. A zero pointer stops the sequence.

6 common animation streams, with entry points $2567 through $25D0. Each five-byte step gives a frame address, signed coordinate deltas and duration. A zero pointer stops the sequence.
Copied from actor offset $05 by $26C0 and incremented as each consecutive VIC sprite pointer is written.
The source selector tested at $2702. Zero uses the $8000 library. A nonzero value uses the stage library at $E000.
Waits for raster line $E1, updates player and enemy sprites, writes the aggregate enable mask, then spends delay loops for unused sprite slots.
Zero initializer before the sprite batch counter in COD1.
Total hardware sprites processed in the current raster update, then reused to count delay iterations.
Count of components in the actor currently being written to VIC registers.
For an active record, copies its frames, publishes coordinates and pointers and fills the actor's consecutive sprite colours.
Writes each X and Y coordinate to its hardware slot, using per-sprite bit masks to set or clear the ninth horizontal bit in $D010.
Reads starting VIC pointer, count and slot from the actor record and writes consecutive pointers into $53F8.
Low byte of the selected library address used to patch the sprite copy.
High byte of the selected source for the sprite copy. The subsequent bytes up to $26EA are zero in COD1.
Reads sprite indices from the actor record, selects the $8000 or $E000 source library and prepares the source pointer and VIC cache destination before copying each frame.
Multiplies the current sprite index by 64 and combines the result with source base $8000.
Calculates the source of the current stage-specific sprite by adding $E000 to its 64-byte index offset.
Count of frame components copied so far.
Number of frame components to copy, taken from actor offset $18.
VIC pointer used to index the destination address table.
Index of the next sprite number within the actor record. Three zero bytes follow before the cache address table.
Eight little-endian slot addresses spaced 64 bytes apart from $7E00 to $7FC0.
Returns the low byte in A and high byte in Y of the unsigned sprite index multiplied by 64.
The zero byte after the multiply-by-64 helper return and before its temporary index.
Index shifted right twice to obtain the source address high part.
Low byte of the VIC cache destination patched into the copy instruction.
High byte of the selected cache address.
Patches the source and destination operands, then uses byte position and pixel-bit permutations to copy a horizontally mirrored sprite.

High byte of the mirrored copy source. The code then translates the byte and indexes the destination permutation.
Low byte of the mirrored sprite destination operand at $27B3.
High byte of that destination. X is then decremented until the 64-byte copy finishes.
Destination permutation for the 64-byte sprite copy at $27B0. The pixel byte order reverses within each row.
Three stored bytes between the 64-entry row-reversal table and the 256-entry pixel reversal table.
256-entry lookup reverses four two-bit pixels within the source byte to mirror the sprite horizontally.
Patches the source at $2917 and destination at $291E, then copies the full 64-byte sprite slot in reverse index order.
Self-modified low address for the unmirrored frame source.
Self-modified high address for the unmapped source slot, followed by the four NOPs before the write.
Patched low byte of the unmirrored sprite cache destination.
The high byte of the unmirrored destination. The next instructions decrement X until the slot is copied.
Five header pointers, beginning at $217D, indexed in the auxiliary actor animation logic.
Four further header pointers starting at $23B4 and covering common actor animation actions.
Table region with action thresholds and common animation header pointers used to set the auxiliary actor's next action.
Burns cycles in an X countdown from $FF when the actor frame routine has no active record.
Adds two packed-BCD score bytes into the three-byte score at $0D11–$0D13 and redraws all six digits before clearing the increment.
Shows the message at $3D46, then resets the stage index, reloads the first five files and returns to the initial three-life setup.
The 15-cell NEXT STAGE banner in the panel character set.
Fifteen character cells saved from the panel by $2A81 before an overlay.
Fifteen saved colour cells corresponding to $2A13.
Places the next-stage caption on the panel and writes the stage number as a panel glyph.
Copies 15 character and colour bytes into the corresponding panel cells at $50AA and $D8AA.
Nine character codes spelling GAME OVER, copied to the panel by $2A91.
Backs up a 15-cell panel strip and its colours and overlays the nine-character GAME OVER message.
Runs the common frame update and VIC sprite update, with a short delay.
Low byte of the stage-specific branch target used by the indirect jump at $2C86.
High byte of the stage-specific opponent callback.
Gate for the first timer-dependent opponent choice in the stage callbacks.
Gate for the second opponent choice, tested after the first branch.
Absolute separation used to decide whether to change the opponent facing bit.
Five bytes indexed by stage, written to offset $1F of the stage actor.
Five values copied to stage actor offset $1E, later used when checking the player/opponent separation.
If the second actor slot is clear, seeds flags, energy, colour and per-stage attributes, then enters the opponent update path at $2E13.
Return instruction immediately before the lane of stage callback pointers at $2C8A.
Five interleaved pointers for the opponent routines selected by stage number before the indirect jump through $2B26.
Toggle used to vary stage callback choices, inverted in stage 1 and stage 4 logic.
Uses the stage flags and CIA1 timer register bits to pick a transition into the opponent action, or leaves the timer path alone.
Uses the CIA1 timer's low two bits to select the special branch when the stage option at $2B28 is enabled.
Varies the special opponent branch by both the timer register and the player's current action class at $11C8.
Uses the player action class, a toggle and timer bits to choose one of two opponent actions.

Option bytes gate the timer-dependent branches. The first can select $2D6B from bit zero of CIA1 timer A high. The follow-up uses that bit to select an index. With both options clear, execution jumps directly to $2E13.
Uses the stage actor directory to choose the opponent's next scripted action and reload its starting duration.
On the $FF action sentinel, reads the actor pointer from $CB0C, follows it to the first frame step and sets the duration counter.
When set, the scroll routine bypasses its alternating displacement branch.
Allows $C087 to adjust the player X during interlude scrolling.
Updated by the interlude sequence at $2F22. Two bytes separate it from the interlude entry.
Enables the flag at $2E71, increases the stage scroll limit by 20 columns and selects the zero-delay scroll path.
Sets the opponent's action sentinel, starting coordinates, enable bytes and stage-specific flag field.
Saves the first auxiliary actor's scroll permission for combination with the second.
Proximity offset taken from the actor and applied on either side of the player.
Tests each eligible actor against the player and combines their flags with the scroll request to decide whether scrolling can continue.
Tests the opponent occupancy flags and a seven-unit horizontal band around the player, then sets actor proximity and scroll permission.
Number of displayed components in the first auxiliary actor, used to place both spritesets in the cache.
Second auxiliary actor count used with the first to detect the six-component case.
Computes the visible sprite counts of both auxiliary actors and redistributes VIC cache slots when they total six.
Loads the second auxiliary actor's header from $19D5, follows it to the first step, and sets the actor to its stage colour.
Reads active actor state and records the hardware sprite count used by the allocation routine.
Attack point horizontal position, combining actor and attack offset.
Attack point vertical position, combining actor and attack offset.
One horizontal attack-box bound before wrapping checks.
Inclusive upper vertical interval bound.
Other horizontal attack-box bound.
Exclusive lower vertical interval bound.
Counter initialised to two for the attack-testing loop.
Selects which repeated-hit flag is tested on the player.
Passes each selected target record to $31D3 with the player as the source actor.
Initializes a two-pass hit-testing path and computes attack coordinates from the attack index and the actor's base position and facing.
Set by a successful point-in-box test.
Tests the point against the vertical interval and handles both ordinary and wrapping horizontal intervals. Sets $32FE on overlap.
Zero initializer after the box test and before the player-hit routine.
Rejects a repeated hit using separate player flag bits and requires both actor enable flags. Sets the corresponding flag, starts a SID effect and reads the current actor header.
Clears panel text, fetches the first stage actor's header pointer from $CB00 and follows it to an animation or state record.
Zero initializer preceding the damage and health bar temporaries.
Low five bits from attacker field $1F, subtracted from the target health.
Result of the subtraction, used by the death check and the health display.
Quotient of the health value divided by four.
Remainder modulo four, selecting a partial bar glyph.
Debounces the hit flag, subtracts the attacker damage field from health, redraws the health bar and chooses a reaction or the death animation.
Four glyph codes for the partially filled health cell, selected by the remainder after division by four.
Four packed-BCD words copied by $3385 and $338C into the score increment, indexed by the action header's score class.
Reads the four offsets in the indexed table at $20D3 into the bounding box workspace.
Adds Y to both vertical sides and X to both horizontal sides of the attack box.
Decimal tens of the countdown shown in the TIME panel.
Decimal units, decremented before borrowing from the tens place.
Gates interrupt updates of the time countdown.
Decrements each active timer update before a timer digit changes.

Toggles the low orientation bit in each of the three non-player actor records.
Gates part of the opponent approach after the coarse scroll position reaches $1E.

Index across the four frequency byte planes.

Resets the note index and prescaler for the music player.
